title: Dental Nurse Salary: Award Rates, Casual Loading, and Super Paid on Top
description: Learn how dental nurse salary is calculated under the Nurses Award 2020, including hourly rates, casual loading, and superannuation paid on top. Use our timesheet to estimate your
salarySummary: Based on the Nurses Award 2020, a dental nurse classified as an Enrolled Nurse pay point 1 earns $30.00 per hour, or $1,139.90 per week for 38 hours, with casual loading of 25% and super of 12% paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical dental nurse salary under the Nurses Award?
faqs.a: Under the Nurses Award 2020, a dental nurse classified as an Enrolled Nurse pay point 1 earns $30.00 per hour for full-time or part-time work. Based on 38 hours per week, the weekly pay is $1,139.90, and the annual salary is approximately $59,280 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect dental nurse pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For a dental nurse at $30.00 per hour, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate for dental nurses?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the hourly rate. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, meaning the employer contributes an additional amount to the employee's super fund. For a dental nurse earning $30.00 per hour, the employer pays an extra $3.60 per hour in super.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Dental Nurse Salary Under the Nurses Award

If you are a dental nurse in Australia, your pay is most likely covered by the **Nurses Award 2020**. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes a Pay Guide that sets out minimum rates for classifications such as Enrolled Nurse and Registered Nurse. For a typical dental nurse, the relevant classification is often **Enrolled Nurse pay point 1**, which from 1 August 2026 has a minimum hourly rate of **$30.00** and a weekly rate of **$1,139.90** for 38 ordinary hours.

This page explains how to convert that hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and casual pay, and how superannuation and tax apply.

## How Annual Pay Is Calculated: Hourly × Hours × 52

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time dental nurse working 38 hours per week at $30.00 per hour:

- Annual gross = $30.00 × 38 × 52 = **$59,280**
- Fortnightly gross = $30.00 × 76 = **$2,280**

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It is a useful starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

## Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, award rates are almost always higher. The Nurses Award rate of $30.00 per hour for an Enrolled Nurse is well above the minimum. Always check the relevant award before accepting a job offer – the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool can help.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation Paid on Top

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual dental nurse, you are entitled to a **25% loading** on top of the base hourly rate. This is specified in clause 11.1 of the Nurses Award. For the $30.00 base rate:

- Casual hourly rate = $30.00 × 1.25 = **$37.50**
- Casual weekly (38 hours) = $37.50 × 38 = **$1,425**
- Casual annual = $37.50 × 38 × 52 = **$74,100**

Remember: the loading is added to the base rate, not included in it. When using our [the timesheet](/), you enter the base hourly rate (e.g., $30.00) and then check the casual loading box to see the correct casual pay.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time dental nurse earning $59,280:

- Super contribution = $59,280 × 12% = **$7,113.60 per year**
- This is paid by the employer and does not reduce your take-home pay.

For a casual dental nurse earning $74,100 annually:

- Super contribution = $74,100 × 12% = **$8,892 per year**

Super is calculated on ordinary earnings only – overtime and some allowances may be excluded. Learn more about how super interacts with your pay at [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Fortnightly Pay and Tax Considerations

Most employers pay wages fortnightly. For a full-time dental nurse at $30.00 per hour:

- Fortnightly gross = $30.00 × 76 = **$2,280**
- Fortnightly super (employer contribution) = $2,280 × 12% = **$273.60**

Tax is withheld by your employer using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (reduction thresholds for 2025–26 apply). For a $59,280 annual salary, the estimated tax plus Medicare is around $9,800, leaving a take-home pay of about $49,500 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed breakdown.

## Using the Timesheet to Estimate Your Pay

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and casual equivalents instantly. Just type your rate (e.g., $30.00 for a dental nurse) and tick the casual loading box if applicable. The tool uses the same formula: hourly × hours per week × 52, and shows super and tax estimates.

Remember: the timesheet assumes 38 hours per week unless you change it. It does not account for penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For award-specific rates, always refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

## Key Takeaways for Dental Nurse Salary

- **Award rate**: Enrolled Nurse pay point 1 = $30.00 per hour (38 hours/week)
- **Annual full-time**: $59,280
- **Casual rate**: $37.50 per hour (including 25% loading)
- **Super**: 12% paid on top by employer
- **Fortnightly**: $2,280 gross for full-time

Always check your classification and pay point using the [reference tables](/data) from the Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database. If you are covered by a different award (e.g., Health Professionals and Support Services Award), the rates may differ.

For more on how casual loading works, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page. And for a comparison with other roles, visit [average pay](/topics/average-pay).
